html:
Francisco Macías Nguema was the first president of Equatorial Guinea, ruling from independence in 1968 until 1979 in one of the most violent regimes in modern Africa.

A Fang from Río Muni who had worked for the Spanish administration, he won the 1968 election and soon turned on rivals. He made himself president for life in 1972, banned parties other than his own, closed churches and schools, and had thousands killed. A large share of the people fled abroad, and the cocoa economy collapsed.

In August 1979 his nephew Teodoro Obiang overthrew him. He was tried and shot that September. Obiang's rule kept power within the same family and clan, so the break with the first decade was smaller than it looked.
sum: Francisco Macías Nguema was the first president of Equatorial Guinea, ruling from independence in 1968 until 1979 in one of the most violent regimes in modern Africa.
